AUTHORITY_GAPS_CLOSED.was: Which role may author and publish an evaluation template version.
AUTHORITY_GAPS_CLOSED.resolution: impact_manager may DRAFT. organization_admin PUBLISHES and RETIRES. Three distinct predicates, each exact set inclusion over a one-element set. Retire emerged as a distinct authorized act that R1 had not modelled.

AUTHORITY_GAPS_CLOSED.was: Which role may record criterion INPUTS.
AUTHORITY_GAPS_CLOSED.resolution: Exactly {analyst, impact_manager, organization_admin}, by exact identity, before the governing lock. reviewer excluded, viewer read-only, super_admin excluded. R1 correctly refused to infer this from the two disagreeing repository precedents (canUploadEvidence at analyst level versus isInReviewSet including reviewer); the ratification picks neither — it admits analyst like the first and excludes reviewer unlike the second.

AUTHORITY_GAPS_CLOSED.was: Whether an Evaluate decider may decide an evaluation they created or whose inputs they recorded.
AUTHORITY_GAPS_CLOSED.resolution: No person-inequality is required in Commercial V1. The traceability floor is mandatory instead, and enforcing it required correcting OBJ-4 from an overwriting upsert to an append-only versioned relation.

AUTHORITY_GAPS_CLOSED.was: Evaluate route location: primary area versus project sub-area.
AUTHORITY_GAPS_CLOSED.resolution: The framing was wrong, not just unanswered: HD-11 ratifies TWO route families that both exist — project evaluations and organization templates — and requires no new first-level navigation item. Exact pathnames within the two constrained subtrees are a bounded implementation choice, which is not an authority gap.

AUTHORITY_GAPS_CLOSED.was: Whether RE_U3's WAIT_FOR_WAVE3_CONTRACT still gates broad Evaluate.
AUTHORITY_GAPS_CLOSED.resolution: Broad Evaluate does not depend on Wave3, FIBIU-19 or FIBIU-20. The narrow run-review FIB surface retains its own independent Wave3 dependency and is not annexed. R1's reduction of this to an authority question rather than a data question was correct; HD-15 answers it.

The canonical ledger is now repository-resident at docs/ops/evaluate/EVALUATE_OWNER_RATIFICATIONS_v1.0.0.json. All sixteen ratifications are consumed verbatim and CS-01..CS-19 were verified against them with ZERO contradictions. HD verbatim provenance is no longer an authority gap.

RESIDUAL_NOTES.note: HD-09 states that impact_manager may draft and that publishing or retiring requires organization_admin. It does NOT say whether organization_admin may ALSO draft. This package does not add it by inference, so canDraftEvaluationTemplate is the one-element set {impact_manager}.
RESIDUAL_NOTES.measured_operational_consequence: An organization whose only privileged member is an organization_admin cannot create an Evaluate template at all — it can publish, but there is nothing to publish, because drafting requires an impact_manager. That is a real and reachable state, not a hypothetical.
RESIDUAL_NOTES.why_not_a_gap: The ratified set is complete enough to implement and is faithful to HD-09 as written. Flagged for the owner as a one-line amendment if the intent was that organization_admin may also draft; implementation is NOT blocked meanwhile.
RESIDUAL_NOTES.escalation: Owner ratification amendment, at the owner's discretion.

RESIDUAL_NOTES.note: RAT-EV-03's traceability floor names a 'review' action alongside criterion-input and decision. No HD ratification defines a distinct Evaluate review state or action, and RAT-EV-02 removes reviewer from criterion editing.
RESIDUAL_NOTES.disposition: This package does NOT invent a review action in order to have something to trace. The floor is satisfied for every action that exists (TRACEABILITY_FLOOR.coverage marks review as NONE IN V1), and any future ratified Evaluate review action inherits the same four facts without amendment.
RESIDUAL_NOTES.why_not_a_gap: Nothing is blocked and nothing is assumed. Inventing a review state to match a word in a ratification's rationale would be exactly the kind of inference this lane refuses.

RESIDUAL_NOTES.note: HD-12's bounded platform-support capability does not exist; PR145 is OPEN and DRAFT, measured. See PLATFORM_SUPPORT_DEPENDENCY.
RESIDUAL_NOTES.disposition: Evaluate fails closed: no platform-support read path at all, and no interim one. Evaluate's own correctness does not depend on the platform-admin successor landing.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer writes canDecideEvaluation with hasRole(role,'impact_manager') because it reads as 'impact_manager and above' and is the dominant idiom in lib/auth/permissions.ts (7 of its helpers use that shape).
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: super_admin silently becomes a tenant decider. HD-05 and HD-12 both violated, with no occurrence of the string 'super_admin' anywhere in the diff to notice.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.control: NSB-01, plus test-manifest N-01 and M-01.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer writes canEditEvaluationCriterionResponse with hasRole(role,'analyst') because analyst is the lowest-ranked member of the edit set.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: The predicate is CORRECT for five of six roles — it admits analyst, impact_manager and organization_admin and correctly denies reviewer and viewer — and WRONG for exactly the one role RAT-EV-02 names as excluded: super_admin. A suite asserting that reviewer and viewer are denied passes. This is the most likely single defect in the whole package.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.control: ROLE_MATRIX.enforcement_mechanism.measured_reason, NSB-01, plus test-manifest N-10 and M-09.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer derives an Evaluate role set from isInReviewSet because Evaluate reads as review tooling.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: reviewer is admitted to criterion editing (violating RAT-EV-02) and potentially to deciding (violating HD-05) in a single move.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer collapses the two Evaluate role sets into one helper because they overlap in two of three members.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: Either analyst gains decision authority or analyst loses criterion-edit authority, depending on which set survives.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer keeps R1's upsert model for criterion responses because it is simpler and the UNIQUE key reads naturally.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: RAT-EV-03's traceability floor becomes unenforceable — the actor, role and timestamp of every superseded response are destroyed, and an organization cannot distinguish an author from a later editor.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.control: OBJ-4.R2_CORRECTION, RLS-06, TRACEABILITY_FLOOR, plus test-manifest P-11 and M-07.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer reconstructs role-at-action by joining to current membership at read time instead of storing it.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: A user whose role changed after the act is reported with the wrong role, silently falsifying exactly the record an organization would rely on to audit a stricter SoD policy.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer stores decision_rationale verbatim in audit after_json, because 40+ existing audit verbs carry verbatim content.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: Tenant decision content becomes readable by every platform superadmin through audit_logs_select_member_or_admin. HD-12 violated via the audit trail.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer reuses domain_object_versions for template versions or criterion responses because it fits structurally and needs no DDL.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: Evaluate content lands behind the super_admin read bypass.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer represents SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE as 0, -1, null or NaN.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: A sentinel number is comparable against DecisionPolicy bands, so an all-N/A evaluation silently acquires a recommended outcome and becomes decidable. HD-02 defeated.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.control: ZD-03, ZD-04, plus test-manifest N-02 and M-03.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer validates band totality only in the evaluator, so an unordered stored policy that happens to evaluate correctly is accepted at publication.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: HD-03 constrains the STORED policy. An unordered policy passes, and a later evaluator change can then produce gaps or overlaps that publication should have refused.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer stores a divergence boolean, or a current-response boolean on OBJ-4, 'for query performance'.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: A third value that can disagree with what it summarizes.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer recomputes the recommended outcome at read time instead of reading recommended_outcome_snapshot when rendering a decided evaluation.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: A historical divergence finding can change after the fact.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer treats an UNANSWERED criterion as a governed N/A.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: An empty evaluation reaches READY_FOR_DECISION with a vacuous SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE, and HD-02's block becomes indistinguishable from ordinary incompleteness.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer builds one canManageTemplate helper covering draft, publish and retire.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: HD-09's whole distinction collapses — either impact_manager can publish, which HD-09 forbids, or impact_manager cannot draft, which HD-09 permits.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.control: TEMPLATE_LIFECYCLE.role_bindings.draft_vs_publish_is_a_real_boundary, plus test-manifest N-16, P-12 and M-08.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer migrates lib/pipeline/methodology-review.ts into Evaluate because RE_U3 calls it a CURRENT_IMPLEMENTATION_SUBSET of Evaluate.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: HD-15's carve-out violated; a FIB-governed, FIBIU-20-owned surface is annexed and its SoD precedent disturbed.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An implementer adds an interim platform read path for support 'until the bounded capability arrives', or treats PR145's authority as its implementation.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: RLS is correct but the runtime reads nothing. Measured precedent: hosted_0007 enumerates 37 tables and 15 FIB tables lack the grant.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.control: RLS-10; carried forward to the ACL successor, not solvable here.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: An independent auditor treats PR106's two audit dispositions as evidence about this package.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: A PASS is inherited that was issued against a different model by reviewers who also did not consult EV-02.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.risk: Zero browser E2E exists, so no Evaluate journey can be proven end-to-end in a browser.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.control: Recorded, not solved. Node-level journey coverage is what the test manifest commits to; a browser harness is a separate, pre-existing repository gap.
